title: Normalize lease telemetry and tighten eviction fastpath
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: The current GPU lease lifecycle code has multiple telemetry shapes emitted from different reconciler paths (legacy leasepool, fastpath, and quarantine). This makes alerting and postmortem analysis noisy and prevents us from accurately measuring eviction latency and root-cause of preemptions. Additionally, the eviction fastpath includes race-prone code that bypasses metrics enrichment and can leave leases in transient orphaned states under heavy churn.

Goal: Consolidate lease telemetry to a single schema, instrument the eviction fastpath so it emits identical lifecycle events as the main reconciler, and refactor the fastpath to eliminate a handful of known races that lead to orphaned allocations. Deliverables: 1) unified telemetry schema and translation layer, 2) eviction fastpath emits lifecycle events and tags (reason, initiator, preemptible), 3) safety guards to prevent orphaned lease state, 4) performance regression test demonstrating <=1% p95 latency impact under synthetic churn, 5) rollout plan with gradual traffic ramp and rollback hooks.
acceptance_criteria: 1) All lease transition events (ALLOCATED, ASSIGNED, EVICTING, EVICTED, RECLAIMED) are emitted from both reconciler and fastpath with the same field names and tagging. 2) No new 'orphaned' lease alerts after a 24h soak on staging under scaled churn (1000 node churn/simulation). 3) p95 request latency change for assignment path < 1% in bench harness. 4) Metrics dashboard updated and new alert thresholds documented. 5) Code review approvals from infra and reliability leads.
technical_notes:
Plan to add a small telemetry facade in pkg/lease/telemetry.go that normalizes fields and persists provenance. Fastpath will call the same facade; reconciler will migrate to it. To avoid allocation overhead, facade will accept an optional pre-built attributes struct (reused from sync.Pool) and only convert to map for legacy sinks. We'll also add a compare-and-swap guard around the fastpath orphan-handling path to ensure only one goroutine advances a lease to EVICTING, and add idempotent reconciliation for leases in TRANSIENT states.

Risk/tradeoffs: Adding the facade introduces a small allocation unless pool reuse covers it; we'll benchmark both pooled and zero-copy paths. Tightening the fastpath may slightly increase critical-path latency; that's why the <=1% p95 target is required. Backward compatibility: implement a translation layer for metric names prefixed with "legacy_" to avoid breaking dashboards during rollout.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature branch and unit tests. 2) Canary deploy to staging autoscaler (10% traffic) for 2 hours with synthetic churn harness. 3) If stable, expand to staging full traffic for 24h soak. 4) Canary deploy to production control plane in one region (us-west-2) with 1h observation window. 5) Gradual ramp to 25%/50%/100% over 48h with automated rollback on alert triggers (orphaned-lease > 5 per 10m or assignment-p95 increase > 3%).
migration_steps: 1) Deploy telemetry facade in compatibility mode (emit both old and new metric names). 2) Update dashboards and alerts to read new names while keeping old to reduce noise. 3) Switch fastpath to call facade behind a feature flag. 4) Disable legacy emissions after 72h of successful production runs and then remove legacy translation in next minor release.
risks:
- Slight latency regression on hot path if pool reuse is insufficient.
- Unexpected alert noise during translation period.
- Edge cases where third-party sinks rely on legacy fields; communicate via #infra-alerts prior to removal.
